svg.text: Mini Feeder — carrier PCB, one-sheet schematic reference (companion to pcb-schematic.md)
Net names in CAPITALS are net labels — connect same-named pins in EasyEDA; wires are only drawn inside each block
→ D3 SS34 ─▶│─ XIAO 5V pin (USB + PSU now safe together)
→ J3 pin1 / J4 pin1 (pH and EC modules)
C5 10u at IN, C6 22u at OUT
USB-C on the XIAO stays reachable.
Bus pull-ups (one pair total): R6 4k7 I2C_SDA→+3V3P · R7 4k7 I2C_SCL→+3V3P
gate pull-downs hold pumps off at boot.
J4 EC module: identical network — R11/R12 10k 1%, C13 100n → EC_DIV → U5 AIN1
2:1 divider matches ADC_DIVIDER_RATIO = 2.0 in config.h; RC corner ≈ 300 Hz.
Sensor modules stay external (BNC + trimmers); they plug in and run from +5V.
Keep this corner of the board away from pump return current — layout rule #1.
5 · PUMP DRIVER — one of four identical channels
Optional per channel: +12V → 2k2 → LED → drain (lights while running)
Safety notes carried from the breadboard build:
· 100k pull-downs are what hold pumps off from reset until I²C is up — never omit
· Logic-level FETs only (AO3400A); an IRF540N will not turn on from 3.3 V
· One pump runs at a time (firmware queue) — 12 V traces sized for one motor + margin
· 12 V + pump traces ≥1.5 mm; pump return routes to C1/jack, not through the board
Identical for TRB → ENC_B (R4/C8) and PSH → ENC_SW (R5/C9).
Place the RC at the XIAO end of the trace. This is the permanent fix for the
encoder interrupt storms: stiff pull-ups + bounce/EMI filtering in copper.
firmware log here even when USB dies.
SJ2: KO → GND, open by default (close if module uses KO as encoder common)
M3 mounting holes ×4 · USB-C aperture clear · display header at board edge
Power block on one edge, analog on the opposite edge, MCU between.
Full pin tables, values, layout rules and the first-power-up checklist: docs/pcb-schematic.md · firmware needs zero changes — nets match include/config.h
